concepts.title: What Drew Europeans to India
concepts.definition: Spices, fine cotton cloth, silk and indigo pulled European merchants across the seas to India from the fifteenth century; Portuguese, Dutch, French and English companies competed for these profitable trades, fighting each other for ports and privileges.
concepts.key_idea: India's spices and textiles were the magnet; trade rivalry was the engine of European arrival.
concepts.textbook_ref: hees104.txt lines 20-110 (what drew European traders, age of colonialism)
question_patterns: which Indian goods attracted European traders
name the European powers that traded with India
why did European companies fight each other in India
how did trade turn into territorial ambition
what was the role of spice trade in European expansion
compare the Portuguese and English arrival in India

solution_steps.explain: Pepper and spices, cotton textiles and indigo fetched high profits in Europe.
Chartered companies monopolised the trade and armed themselves.
Rivalry for ports and privileges pulled Europeans into Indian politics.

concepts.title: The English East India Company
concepts.definition: Chartered in 1600, the English East India Company built trading factories at Madras, Bombay and Calcutta, kept its own army, and used diplomacy and war to bend Indian rulers, transforming from a trading body into a territorial power.
concepts.key_idea: A company with an army: trade posts at Madras, Bombay and Calcutta grew into an empire.
concepts.textbook_ref: hees104.txt lines 67-110 (English East India Company, Madras Bombay and Calcutta), 400-475
question_patterns: when and why was the English East India Company formed
name the three presidency cities of the English company
how did a trading company build its own army
what rights did the company obtain from Indian rulers
how did the company's factories grow into fortified settlements
describe the transformation of the company from trader to ruler

solution_steps.explain: The 1600 charter gave the company a monopoly of English trade in the East.
Madras, Bombay and Calcutta became fortified trading headquarters.
Recruiting sepoys and waging wars made the company a political power.

concepts.title: Battle of Plassey and Company Rule
concepts.definition: The Battle of Plassey in 1757 gave the English company control over Bengal's riches, and victories that followed - Buxar and the annexation of Punjab - step by step converted commercial footholds into direct colonial rule over India.
concepts.key_idea: Plassey 1757 is the hinge: from revenue-rich Bengal the company annexed India province by province.
concepts.textbook_ref: hees104.txt lines 109-130 (Battle of Plassey, company annexes Punjab), 474-540 (Plassey 1757 in focus)
question_patterns: what happened at the Battle of Plassey
who led the English at Plassey and who was defeated
how did the victory at Plassey change the company's position
why is the Battle of Plassey a turning point in Indian history
how did the company annex Punjab
trace the steps by which the company became ruler of India

solution_steps.explain: In 1757 company forces defeated the nawab of Bengal, aided by conspiracy.
Revenue of Bengal financed further conquests, sealing control after Buxar.
Wars and annexations, including Punjab, completed the colonial map by the mid-1800s.

concepts.title: Life under Colonial Rule: Portuguese Rule and Europeans in India
concepts.definition: Colonialism reshaped Indian life: the Portuguese enforced religious policies in their enclaves, European settlements changed coastal cities, and exploitative land taxes and trade rules drained Indian wealth while drawing India into a world empire.
concepts.key_idea: Colonial rule meant political control plus economic drain and cultural pressure.
concepts.textbook_ref: hees104.txt lines 187-300 (Europeans in India, Portuguese policies)
question_patterns: how did Portuguese rule affect the people of their territories
what was the economic impact of colonial rule on India
how did European settlements change Indian coastal cities
define colonialism in the Indian context
why is the colonial era called exploitative
describe the social changes brought by Europeans in India

solution_steps.explain: Indian rulers lost sovereignty to company and crown rule.
Heavy taxation, forced crops and one-way trade drained India's wealth.
Missionary activity, new laws and western education reshaped urban life.
